chunks: And by this chain, he said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: There is no interest (usury) between us and the people who war against us. We can take a thousand Dirhams from them with one Dirham, and we can take from them and we cannot give them.

key_terms.أَلْفَ دِرْهَمٍ بِدِرْهَمٍ: A thousand Dirhams for one Dirham; an idiom for taking a large amount for a small amount.
key_terms.أَهْلِ حَرْبِنَا: The people of war; non-Muslims with whom Muslims are in a state of conflict.
key_terms.رِبًا: Usury or interest; specifically referring to the strict financial prohibition in Islamic law.
key_terms.وَلَا نُعْطِيَهُمْ: And we do not give them; indicating the one-way nature of the transaction.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Riba (usury) in transactions with non-Muslims during war?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the juristic principle of 'taking but not giving' (أخذ ولا إعطاء), where the strict reciprocity required in Riba is waived when dealing with non-Muslims in a state of war. It reflects the Shia scholarly view that the prohibition of usury is primarily a protective measure for Muslims, allowing for greater flexibility in extracting wealth from enemies without the obligation of equivalent return. This distinction underscores the pragmatic application of financial laws in the context of conflict and tribute.
